tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room: full room-type→assemblies system
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite scaffold already in B1. Full version: room_type → up to 8 CSI quantities (paint/drywall/flooring/ceiling) using CSI libraries + wall heights. Last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the full `room_type→assemblies` system in `engine/assemblies.py`: classification → quantities (paint/drywall/flooring) + wall heights, producing estimator-grade Excel with CSI-formula quantities per room.
prep.understand: The `assemblies-lite` scaffold was already folded into B1 as a thin stub. The full version maps each detected `room_type` to up to 8 CSI quantities using `csi_libraries` — paint coverage, drywall area, flooring area, ceiling area, etc. Wall heights are needed for wall-area quantities (not in the 2D plan; use a project-level default). This is Phase 6, actively `in_progress`, and it is the last pillar that unlocks the estimator-grade Excel export. Everything else in the pipeline is ready; this is the missing computation.
approach: Open `engine/assemblies.py` — review the existing scaffold, find what's stubbed vs implemented
Design (or finalize) the `room_type → assemblies` mapping dict with each assembly type's CSI formula and default wall height
Implement quantity derivation per room: paint coverage (wall SF = perimeter × height), drywall (same SF), flooring (floor area from polygon), ceiling (floor area)
Wire the assembled quantities into `build_sheet_takeoff` in `engine/excel.py` and run an end-to-end test with a known-geometry room to verify the Excel output

CSI MasterFormat reference for material category codes

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on the Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text. v2 = (a) productize M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action; (b) callout-vs-room filtering (general-note paragraphs, UP arrows, FEC callouts).

prep.what: Add an opt-in 'Read labels (AI)' endpoint using the M3 tiles lane, and add callout-vs-room filtering to stop general notes/arrows from being misread as room names.
prep.understand: PDFTron-generated PDFs outline ALL text as vector paths — the free live-text lane finds zero room names on them. The M3 tiles lane (spike: `run_labels_m3tiles.py`) CAN read outlined text but it's expensive (~4.3 min/sheet, costs money via MINIMAX_AI). Two-part fix: (a) expose it as an OPT-IN action (not auto-run — avoids unexpected charges, maps to the §7a metered-credits event in the PRD); (b) clean up noise on firms where the text lane already works: Holabird shows general paragraphs, 'UP' stair arrows, and FEC callouts getting matched as room names.
approach: Review `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` to understand the M3 tiles pipeline and what the service needs to call it
Add a `POST /sheets/{sheet_id}/read-labels` endpoint as an opt-in action: calls the M3 tiles lane, stores labels back to `Measurement` rows, requires `MINIMAX_AI` key in env

For callout filtering in the live-text lane: add heuristics before storing — filter general paragraphs (>40 chars), single-word directionals (`UP`, `DN`), alphanumeric callout patterns (`FEC`, `AHU-1`) using regex
Run `pytest service/` — verify the existing tests stay green; add a test for the callout filter with at least one false-positive example
resources: STATE.md (VPS secrets section — MiniMax key placement)

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter × height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall/ceiling height input (project default + optional per-room override); wall paint SF/room = perimeter × height. Seeder currently DROPS geometry — preserve it.

prep.what: Add a `wall_height_ft` column to estimates, preserve `geometry.rings` + `meta.perimeter` from the engine response in `TakeoffEstimateSeeder`, and emit a 'Wall paint area' line item per room using `perimeter × wall_height`.
prep.understand: The engine returns per-room data including `meta.perimeter` (room perimeter in feet) and `geometry.rings` (polygon data). `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` currently drops geometry entirely — that's the bug. The missing piece is height: a 2D plan doesn't encode wall height, so you need a user-supplied default (e.g. 8ft) stored on the estimate with optional per-room override. `wall_area_sqft = perimeter × height`. The painting labor rate seeder row already exists. This unlocks real painting estimates for CT Pros' primary trade.
approach: Create a migration: add `wall_height_ft` (float, nullable, default 8.0) to the `estimates` table; add fillable + accessor to `Estimate.php`
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop dropping engine geometry: preserve `meta.perimeter` and `geometry.rings` on each room measurement
Derive wall area per room: `wall_area_sqft = $room['meta']['perimeter'] * ($estimate->wall_height_ft ?? 8.0)`, then call `LineItemFactory` to emit a painting area line item
Add `wall_height` input to the Takeoff or Estimate edit form (numeric, defaults to 8ft), wire it to `estimates.wall_height_ft`
Add a test: seed a takeoff with a known-perimeter room + 8ft height → verify wall_area = perimeter × 8
resources: app/Services/TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php (start here — find where geometry is dropped)
database/migrations/ (reference a recent migration for format)

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind+geometry. Preserve+switch on kind: area(SF)->flooring, derived wall SF->painting, line(LF)->wall-linear/trim, count(EA)->doors/tile.

prep.what: Modify `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` to route each measurement `kind` to the correct trade instead of collapsing everything into anonymous `kind=custom $0` lines.
prep.understand: The engine returns each room measurement with a `kind` field: `area` (SF floors), `line` (LF trim/wall-linear), `count` (EA doors/fixtures). Right now all of them get dumped into a single custom line losing the info entirely. After t45 adds wall-area derivation, you have: `area(SF)` → flooring rate, derived wall SF → painting rate, `line(LF)` → per-LF trim rate (t47 done), `count(EA)` → doors/tile. Use `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` to tag each line with the right trade.
approach: In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, add a switch on measurement `kind`: case `'area'` → `LineItemFactory` with flooring rate; case `'line'` → `LineItemFactory` with `PerLinearFt` rate; case derived wall SF → painting rate
Tag each line item with the appropriate trade using `ProjectType::group()` / `isCoreTrade()` from `app/Enums/ProjectType.php`
Set `is_subcontracted = true` for non-core trades (tile, trim) per `isCoreTrade()` — flooring and painting stay own-team
Add/update a seeder test: fixture with area+line+count measurements produces correctly typed and trade-tagged line items

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' + label, wire LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType->'lf', seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing (t48).

prep.what: Add a new `PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft'` case to the `RateType` enum, wire it into `unitFromRateType` in `LineItemFactory`, and seed a per-LF trim `LaborRate` row.
prep.understand: `RateType` controls how estimate line items are priced and what unit label they get. No per-linear-foot rate exists yet. This is the prerequisite for t48 (pricing seeded takeoff trim/wall-linear lines) — if this isn't in before t46 runs, LF measurements have nothing to key on.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` case with a label to `app/Enums/RateType.php`
Wire it in `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` to return `'lf'` as the unit string
Add a per-LF trim `LaborRate` seed row in `database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php`
Run `php artisan test --filter=LaborRate` to confirm no regressions
